title: A day in Capernaum (Mark 1:21–39)
hookLine: teaching, healing late into the night, and before dawn he goes out alone to pray

cards: Capernaum, a fishing town on the lake. Mark gives one day there almost hour by hour, and it doesn't let up. Morning in the synagogue.
Afternoon at Simon's house. Evening, the whole town at the door. Every hour, someone needs something.
It's the kind of day that ends in the dark with no memory of lunch. And then, the next morning, before anyone is awake, a detail that shows how Jesus met a day like that.

teach.b: First, the morning. It's the sabbath, and Jesus teaches in the synagogue. People are astonished, Mark says, because he teaches as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
Mark doesn't spell out the difference. A man with an unclean spirit cries out, and Jesus silences the spirit and sends it out. Second, the afternoon, at the house of Simon and Andrew.
Simon's mother-in-law is in bed with a fever.

teach.h: AFTERNOON: A HAND, AND THE FEVER GOES.
teach.b: Jesus goes to her, takes her by the hand, and lifts her up, and the fever leaves her. That small detail tells you something else: Peter had a wife. Third, the evening.
Mark notes that the sun has set, and some readers connect that to the sabbath ending.

teach.h: EVENING: THE WHOLE TOWN AT THE DOOR.
teach.b: The sick are brought, and the whole town gathers at the door. Mark says he healed many.

teach.h: AND RISING VERY EARLY, THERE HE PRAYED.
teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "And rising very early, going out, he went into a desert place: and there he prayed." After a day like that, before anyone's up, he slips out alone.
Mark doesn't tell us what he prayed, only that he went. And they come hunting for him. Simon finds him and says, almost impatiently: "All seek for thee."
Jesus doesn't go back to the crowd. Let's go on to the next towns, he says, so I can preach there too; that's why I came. In Capernaum today, pilgrims visit a house that tradition says was Peter's.

how: Catholics may begin the day with Morning Prayer from the Liturgy of the Hours or a morning offering, and in monasteries the first prayers of the day are sung before dawn.

games.q: you had the biggest day yet. the whole town loves you, and in the morning Simon finds you and says: all seek for thee. what do you do?
o: go back to Capernaum, where everyone's waiting.
move on to the next towns to preach there too.
games.why: Jesus says let's go into the next towns; that's why he came. he doesn't stay where he's most wanted.

practice: If it's morning where you are, good; if not, imagine it's tomorrow, before the alarm, before the phone, and picture a quiet place like the deserted spot where Jesus went. Nothing to answer yet, nobody seeking you yet.
If you pray, simply be with God there without asking for anything; if you don't, just rest in the quiet before the day's first demand.

wordCard.voice: Capernaum. The lake town where Jesus worked a full day, from synagogue to sickbed to the crowded door, and then prayer before dawn. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek spelling of Capernaum, usually explained as the Hebrew Kfar Nahum, the village of Nahum.

carryVoice: Your line: rising very early. After the crowded door, a quiet place. That's day one hundred ninety-five.

sources.q: And rising very early, going out, he went into a desert place: and there he prayed.
